papers.title_in_file: A Survey of Quantum Transformers: Architectures, Challenges and Outlooks
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction (first part), challenges and outlook passages by search, Conclusion; not the per-architecture sections
papers.what_it_is: A survey of quantum Transformer models, organized into PQC-based and QLA-based paradigms.

assertions.value: The authors state that they organize existing quantum Transformer studies into two main paradigms, PQC-based and QLA-based.
quotes: we organize existing studies into two main paradigms: Parameterized Quantum Circuits (PQC)-based and Quantum Linear Algebra (QLA)-based
assertions.certainty_reason: The survey's own statement of its taxonomy, Abstract p.1

assertions.value: The authors state that the survey summarizes empirical results that demonstrate preliminary quantum advantages, especially on small-scale tasks or resource-constrained settings.
quotes: We also summarize empirical results that demonstrate preliminary quantum advantages, especially on small-scale tasks or resource-constrained settings.
assertions.certainty_reason: A survey's summary of results from other studies
assertions.reader_inference: The abstract calls the advantages preliminary and limited to small scale.

assertions.value: The authors state that QLA-based quantum Transformer models generally do not support parameter updates, which results in static, inference-oriented architectures.
quotes: but generally do not support parameter updates, resulting in static, inference-oriented architectures
assertions.certainty_reason: A survey-level characterization of a class of models

assertions.value: The authors state that key technical challenges are complexity-resource trade-offs, scalability and generalization limitations, and trainability issues including barren plateaus.
quotes: we examine key technical challenges
assertions.certainty_reason: The survey's own list of open challenges

papers.title_in_file: Benchmarking Agents for Proving Theorems in Quantum Algorithms and Quantum Information
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction (first part), Section 7 Discussion and Conclusion, results lines by search
papers.what_it_is: Two Lean 4 theorem-proving benchmarks for AI agents on quantum algorithms and quantum information theory, with a four-model evaluation.

assertions.value: The authors report that on two Lean 4 benchmarks of 36 and 40 theorem-completion tasks, the highest difficulty-weighted scores are 60.4 out of 100 for quantum algorithms and 59.6 out of 100 for quantum information.
quotes: two Lean 4 benchmarks containing 36 and 40 theorem-completion tasks for quantum algorithms and quantum information theory
The highest difficulty-weighted scores are 60.4 out of 100 on the quantum-algorithm benchmark and 59.6 out of 100 on the quantum-information benchmark.
assertions.certainty_reason: Single-run empirical result

assertions.value: The authors report that library-augmented deduction (LAD) improves both score and completion rate in all eight model-benchmark comparisons, with gains of up to 15.9 points.
quotes: LAD improves both score and completion rate in all eight
with gains of up to 15.9 points
assertions.certainty_reason: Single-run empirical result; baseline and LAD runs not fully matched

assertions.value: The authors state that each suite-model-condition combination has one run, so the results give no estimate of stochastic variation, and that the 36 and 40 tasks do not provide complete coverage of either domain.
quotes: so the results provide no estimate of stochastic variation
Their 36 and 40 tasks do not provide complete coverage of either domain
assertions.certainty_reason: Section 7.1, p.14

papers.title_in_file: Enhancing Quantum Machine Learning with Anyons
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction (first part), Section VI Discussion and Outlook
papers.what_it_is: A quantum kernel framework that unifies bosonic, fermionic and anyonic exchange statistics, evaluated on MNIST and Fashion-MNIST.

assertions.value: The authors report that anyonic kernels consistently outperform their bosonic and fermionic counterparts on learning benchmarks, with stronger target alignment and more favorable class geometry.
quotes: anyonic kernels consistently
with stronger target alignment and more favorable class geometry
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result on a few datasets, simulated

assertions.value: The authors state that Haar-averaged effective-dimension analysis shows fractional exchange phases access feature-space directions inaccessible to the purely symmetric or antisymmetric limits.
quotes: fractional exchange phases access feature-space directions inaccessible to the purely symmetric or antisymmetric limits
assertions.certainty_reason: Analysis result stated in the abstract; details not checked

assertions.value: The authors state that the two-particle regime is accessible with existing technology, and that extending to larger particle numbers will require multipartite entangled inputs and mode-matched optical networks.
assertions.anchor: Section VI Discussion and Outlook, p.12
quotes: The two-particle regime is therefore directly accessible with existing technology.
Extending the approach to larger particle numbers will require multipartite entangled inputs
assertions.certainty_reason: Section VI, pp.12-13

papers.title_in_file: Experimental robustness benchmarking of quantum neural networks on a superconducting quantum processor
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction (first part), Conclusion, Method (training section)
papers.what_it_is: An experiment benchmarking adversarial robustness of 20-qubit QNN classifiers on a superconducting processor.

assertions.value: The authors report that adversarial training mitigates sensitivity to targeted perturbations by regularizing input gradients, significantly enhancing QNN robustness.
quotes: adversarial training mitigates sensitivity to targeted perturbations by regularizing input gradients, thereby significantly enhancing QNN robustness
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical hardware result on two small datasets

assertions.value: The authors report that experimentally measured QNNs exhibit higher adversarial robustness than classical neural networks, an effect they attribute to inherent quantum noise.
quotes: experimentally measured QNNs exhibit higher adversarial robustness than classical neural net-
an effect attributed to inherent quantum noise
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical comparison against one classical network
assertions.reader_inference: The paper itself frames the effect as noise acting as gradient masking, not as a security gain.

assertions.value: The authors state that adversarial training cannot provide universal protection and that absolute robustness is unattainable for non-trivial classifiers.
quotes: cannot provide universal protection
absolute robustness is unattainable for non-trivial classifiers
assertions.certainty_reason: An argued limitation, not tested in the paper

papers.title_in_file: Expressibility and trainability of a two-dimensional pairwise quantum-circuit ansatz
papers.what_it_is: A numerical comparison of a native 2D pairwise ansatz with three 1D ansatze on expressibility and gradient variance.

assertions.value: The authors report that for the fixed 16-qubit system the 2D ansatz has the smallest KL divergence at L = 1 and 2.
quotes: For the fixed 16-qubit system, the 2D ansatz has the smallest KL divergence at L = 1 and 2
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerical result for one system size

assertions.value: The authors report that the gradient variance of the Pauli-Z string is smaller for the 2D circuit at low layer counts, that the differences narrow at L = 5, and that the four ansatze yield statistically compatible variances at L = 6.
quotes: the gradient variance is smaller for the 2D circuit
The differences narrow at L = 5, and the four ansatze yield statistically compatible variances at L = 6.
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerical result for one observable and one parameter

assertions.value: The authors state that the result is for one observable, one parameter and one system size, N = 16, and does not test barren-plateau scaling with system size.
quotes: This is a result for one observable, one parameter, and one system size.
Because only N = 16 is studied, the calculation does not test barren-plateau scaling with system size.
assertions.certainty_reason: Section V, pp.22-23

papers.title_in_file: A Theory of Finite-Noise Optima and Generalization in Quantum Machine Learning
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction (first part), Section III Discussion
papers.what_it_is: A statistical learning theory linking quantum noise to generalization, predicting a finite-noise optimum, with numerical checks.

assertions.value: The authors state that a noise-order purity parameter, derived from a surrogate model analysis, predicts the noise-induced reduction in model complexity and the consequent reduction in the generalization gap.
quotes: predicts the noise-induced reduction in model complexity and the consequent reduction in the generalization gap
assertions.certainty_reason: Result of a surrogate-model analysis, not a proof about the physical model

assertions.value: The authors state that the finite-noise optimum behaves differently in over- and underparameterized models and can eventually disappear in the large-sample limit.
quotes: can eventually disappear in the large-sample limit
assertions.certainty_reason: Theoretical analysis with a noise-order surrogate and local linearization

assertions.value: The authors state that the present simulations assume independent gate-level noise, and that whether the prediction holds for correlated or time-dependent errors is a hardware question left open.
quotes: The present simulations assume independent gate-level noise.
assertions.certainty_reason: Section III Discussion, p.11

papers.title_in_file: Advantage of Quantum Neural Networks as Quantum Information Decoders
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction (first part), numerical results paragraph, Discussion; proofs not checked
papers.what_it_is: A theory paper proving bounds on decoding perturbed stabilizer codes with standard QEC versus QNN decoders, with small simulations.

assertions.value: The authors state that they prove the standard stabilizer-based decoding error diminishes exponentially in the distance of the underlying unperturbed code.
quotes: showing that the decoding error diminishes exponentially in the distance of the underlying unperturbed code
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorems 1 and 2, as cited in the main text

assertions.value: The authors state that they prove QNN decoders provide an almost quadratic improvement on the readout error.
quotes: We then prove that Quantum Neural Network (QNN) decoders provide an almost quadratic improvement on the readout error.
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorem 3 (lower bound), main text; the QNN reaching it is checked only by simulation
assertions.reader_inference: The proof is a bound on achievable error; the simulations are small.

assertions.value: The authors state that the numerical simulations cover codes with distances ranging from 5 to 11 qubits and that they focus on imperfect stabilizer codes, leaving extension beyond near-stabilizer codes open.
quotes: numerical simulations of codes with various distances ranging from 5 to 11 qubits
While we focus on imperfect stabilizer codes, an immediate question is whether our formalism can be extended beyond near-stabilizer codes.
assertions.certainty_reason: Discussion, p.6

papers.title_in_file: QCDGE database, Quantum Chemistry Database with Ground- and Excited-state Properties of 450 Kilo Molecules
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Background and Summary, Technical Validation (scaffold and functional-group parts), Usage Notes
papers.what_it_is: A classical-DFT quantum-chemistry database of small organic molecules with ground- and excited-state properties, built for machine learning in chemistry.

assertions.value: The authors state that they built a quantum-chemistry database of 443,106 small organic molecules with sizes up to 10 heavy atoms including carbon (C), nitrogen (N), oxygen (O), and fluorine (F).
quotes: includes 443,106 small organic molecules
with sizes up to 10 heavy atoms including carbon (C), nitrogen (N), oxygen (O), and fluorine (F)
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of the database's own scope, Abstract p.1

assertions.value: The authors state that ground-state optimizations and frequency calculations used B3LYP/6-31G* with the BJD3 dispersion correction, and that excited-state single-point calculations were run at a different level of theory.
quotes: were performed at the B3LYP/6-31G* level with the BJD3 dispersion correction
the excited-state single-point calculations were
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own computational setup, Abstract p.1

assertions.value: The authors state that the absence of certain functional groups may be attributed to the limit on the number of atoms from their selection rule, not to a lack of chemical diversity.
quotes: does not suggest a lack of chemical diversity, while it may be attributed to the limitation on the number of atoms due to our selection rule
assertions.certainty_reason: Technical Validation, functional-group analysis
